description:
PROVENANCE / RESEARCH-INTEGRITY issue under RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md.

crates/outram-park-fork-pflotran is 26,409 lines across 47 .rs files, written WITHOUT ever obtaining the upstream PFLOTRAN source.

Evidence:
- NOTICE:19-25 admits it outright: "LICENSE PROVENANCE -- VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISH. The LGPL-2.1-or-later determination above was taken from the PFLOTRAN documentation and the OSTI/DOECODE records (2026-07-20), not from a byte-for-byte reading of the upstream LICENSE/COPYRIGHT file (which was not reachable from this environment)."
- No upstream clone exists on this machine. /home/teddy0/Documents/research/ has openfoam, openmc, NJOY2016, dwsim, ThermoSysPro -- no pflotran. A find over the filesystem returns only /usr/include/paraview/vtkVisItPFLOTRANReader.h.
- upstream_source/ contains only README.md, which states "It holds no PFLOTRAN source yet".
- No .rs file in src/ carries a provenance header naming an upstream .F90 file, contrary to the workspace attribution rule.

WHY THE GAP IS LOAD-BEARING: the GPL-3.0-only relicensing relies on LGPL-2.1 section 3, which only works if upstream really is LGPL-2.1-OR-LATER and not a bare LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0, or a mixed-file situation. Nobody has read the upstream LICENSE/COPYRIGHT.

SECOND, SEPARATE CONTRADICTION: NOTICE:27-28 says "No PFLOTRAN source has been ported into this crate yet -- it is a documented scaffold", while README.md:55-61 describes RICHARDS flow, transport, energy, geochemistry, kinetics, reactive transport and multiphase as "real (verif-only)" with a 114-test suite. Root Cargo.toml:25-27 and workspace CLAUDE.md also still call it a scaffold. Either 26k LOC was written without upstream -- in which case "fork/translation of PFLOTRAN" is the wrong framing and the crate should be renamed/reframed as an independent implementation informed by published equations -- or code WAS derived and the per-file attribution is missing.

Note README.md:122 marks the provenance bead op-v6s.1 as "done (verify upstream before publish)" -- that should not read as done.

REQUIRED before this crate is published or described as a PFLOTRAN fork:
1. Obtain a PFLOTRAN clone and read LICENSE/COPYRIGHT byte-for-byte; record it in upstream_source/README.md.
2. Decide and state honestly whether this is a derived port (then add per-file provenance headers) or an independent implementation (then stop calling it a fork).
3. Reconcile NOTICE / README / root Cargo.toml / workspace CLAUDE.md so they agree.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.
title: pflotran: 26.4k LOC written without upstream; licence never verified (provenance)

description:
Attempted to compile OpenFOAM Foundation dev (vendored at crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/upstream_source/OpenFOAM) in the Claude Code remote container, in order to run the incompressibleDriftFlux/dahl and multiphaseEuler/bubbleColumn coarse tutorials.

SETUP THAT WORKED: apt-installed flex + OpenMPI; built the wmake bootstrap tools (wmkdep, dirToString) via wmake/src/make; worked around the clone being named "OpenFOAM" while etc/bashrc expects "OpenFOAM-$WM_PROJECT_VERSION" by symlinking /opt/foam/OpenFOAM-dev to the vendored tree -- placed OUTSIDE the repo so build artifacts land in the gitignored dir and git status stays clean. Compilation itself is clean: zero real compile errors across ~1650 objects and 31 libraries.

BLOCKER: long-running background builds do not survive. Two launches died mid-build during idle gaps between turns (first ~35 min in, second ~8 min in). This is NOT resource exhaustion: no OOM entries, 14 GB RAM free, 19 GB disk free. setsid + nohup + detaching to PPID 1 did not help. Measured directly: a 9.3-minute FOREGROUND tool call advanced the build (objects 1618 to 1654, libs 28 to 31), while equivalent idle wall-clock advanced it by zero. Conclusion: the container only executes work while a tool call is active.

COST TO FINISH IN FOREGROUND: ~3800 of 5440 source files remain; at the observed rate in the current template-heavy stage that is roughly 4-16 hours of ACTIVE tool time (~25-100 dedicated 9.5-minute calls doing nothing but waiting). Not a sensible use of a session.

DIAGNOSTIC TRAP (cost an hour): pgrep -f make returns false positives because the claude process's own command line contains the word "make". Check liveness with: ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep '[b]uild2.sh' and require PPID 1.

NOT BLOCKED, ALREADY DELIVERED (commit ce4bd82): the OUTRAM PARK equivalent V&V cases for all three targets, built from the upstream inputs verbatim, all passing -- GeN-Foam 1-D slab k_eff = 1.000008 vs analytical 1.000004 (0.4 pcm); dahl drift-flux settling 1.137e-3 m/s with the upstream simple closure reproduced exactly; bubbleColumn six-equation terminal slip 0.292 m/s with Schiller-Naumann drag.

SUGGESTED RESOLUTION: run the two OpenFOAM tutorials on a normal workstation and commit their reference output (mesh stats, alpha/U/T fields at the reported times) into the repo as stored benchmarks, so the Rust ports can be regression-compared without needing OpenFOAM in CI or in the container. Same pattern as the GeN-Foam/ESI bead.
title: OpenFOAM upstream build not viable in remote container: background jobs reaped on idle

description:
Maintainer reports both fhr_sim_v2 and htgr_sim_v1 feel laggy (2026-08-12). Bearable, so deferred.

RULED OUT (measured, release build): physics (TH loop <20000 us against a 100000 us budget = 20% duty; PRKE <10 us); lock contention (app/mod.rs:134 drops the guard immediately); unbounded growth (plot buffers capped at NUM_DATA_PTS_IN_PLOTS); debug build (confirmed --release).

WHY BOTH SIMS: they share crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/. This demotes op-szmi.9 (per-frame FHRState clone) -- htgr_sim_v1 does not do that clone and lags anyway.

QUANTIFIED LEAD: src/components/pebble_packing.rs bakes 523 pebbles in PACKED_PEBBLES. Each is drawn as one body circle plus a TRISO speckle whose count is triso_dot_count(radius), clamped to 4..=18 (htr10_reactor_vessel.rs:389). So a fully-zoomed vessel emits roughly 523 * 19 = ~10000 circles PER VESSEL PER FRAME, each tessellated to triangles by egui every repaint. Both vessel widgets use this table.

NOTE a doc/code discrepancy found while measuring: pebble_packing.rs module docs (line 124) say each pebble carries 'of order 50 dots, so the circle count is ~50x the pebble count'. The code clamps to 18. Either the doc is stale or the generator and the widget disagree -- worth resolving, since the doc is what a reader sizes the cost from.

FIRST STEP: promote GuiFrameMetrics (examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/gui_frame_metrics.rs, added 2026-08-12) into src/app_scaffold/ so both examples share it, then read the split. Small update() CPU with a long frame interval means the cost is egui tessellation/paint of those circles, and the fix is fewer shapes -- bake the static bed to a texture, or cull occluded pebbles -- NOT optimising our ui() body. Read the split before choosing.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
DESIGN AGREED WITH MAINTAINER 2026-08-12 -- bake to a texture, tint at draw.

Key enabling fact: triso_dot_offset is deterministic by construction (htr10_reactor_vessel.rs:431 documents this explicitly -- it exists to stop the speckle shimmering between frames). The artwork is therefore STATIC across frames. Re-drawing it every repaint is pure waste, not animation.

Do NOT snapshot the finished coloured picture -- temperature changes every frame and would invalidate the cache immediately, buying nothing.

Instead: rasterise the depth-shaded bed ONCE into an egui ColorImage as luminance/alpha, upload via ctx.load_texture, and paint it as a SINGLE textured quad with the temperature colour applied as a multiply tint. Temperature then never invalidates the cache. Per-frame cost goes from ~10000 circles to 4 vertices.

Fill level composes as a CLIP RECT at draw time, not a cache key -- bake the full bed, clip to the fill line.

Cache key: physical pixel size (rect * pixels_per_point), so it re-bakes only on resize or DPI/monitor change.

Cheaper half-measure if the texture route stalls: cache a pre-tessellated egui::Mesh. Skips CPU tessellation but still uploads ~120k vertices per frame. Strictly worse; note it only as a fallback.

Known tradeoff to accept or mitigate: a texture is raster and will resample on resize where the current vector path stays crisp. Keying the bake on PHYSICAL pixels avoids this in the steady state.

Still do the measurement first (promote GuiFrameMetrics to src/app_scaffold/) so the before/after is a number, not a claim.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12 -- bed baked to three luminance/alpha textures, tinted at draw.

New module src/components/pebble_bed_texture.rs. Three masks (backdrop / graphite matrix / TRISO speckle), each painted as a tinted quad; every colour incl. temperature is a vertex tint, so temperature never invalidates the cache. Cache key = physical pixel size + packing scale + crop window + vertical sense; NOT colour, NOT position. BedTint::Axial is built and tested for the future 15-25 zone nodalised bed. Fill level composes as a draw-time clip rect, not a key.

MEASURED (headless egui, release, 2026-08-12, build+tessellate of one whole vessel, median of 20):
  HTR-10 190x400 pt: 19903 -> 32 shapes; 80472 -> 988 vertices; 1.61 -> 0.010 ms
  FHR    225x1050 pt: 9909 -> 32 shapes; 52340 -> 1052 vertices; 0.42 -> 0.012 ms
Bed's own share: 19874 circles -> 3 quads / 12 vertices (HTR-10).
Bake cost paid only on resize: 2.4 ms for a 232x353 px bed at 2x DPI.

DOC/CODE DISCREPANCY RESOLVED: the stale one was htr10_reactor_vessel::triso_dot_count's own doc table ('1.5 * radius, clamped to 4..=18'). The code clamps to 24..=260 and derives the count from TRISO_TARGET_FILL; at the HTGR example size it is 37 dots per pebble. pebble_packing.rs's 'of order 50 dots' module doc was approximately RIGHT, not stale. triso_dot_count's table corrected; pebble_packing.rs left alone (generated file).

GuiFrameMetrics promoted to src/app_scaffold/gui_frame_metrics.rs (re-exported). The example's own copy was left in place so examples/fhr_sim_v2 keeps compiling untouched -- switching it to the engine copy is a one-line follow-up for whoever owns that example.

title: GUI lag in BOTH simulators: 19,874 circles/frame from the shared pebble-bed artwork
